**What this file is.** The clauses this project cites, transcribed from the standard as published, with the
source and the hash of the file read. The standard itself is fetched, not redistributed: the European
Cooperation for Space Standardization publishes it free of charge and it answers this host.

## Why this project reads a SPACE standard for its fuses

Rules PWR-003 and BAT-002 ask what a fuse selection is judged against. The fuses' own datasheets name SAE
J1284 and ISO 8820-3, neither of which is free, and the makers' selection guides are behind a host that refuses
this one. This standard publishes a derating criterion for fuses with its numbers, free, from a body whose
documents this project already cites (ECSS-Q-ST-70-12C for the board rules, ECSS-E-HB-20-07A for EMC).

**And it says plainly what it does NOT cover**, which is why the citation is bounded, below.

## 6.17.1 General (Fuses: Cermet, family-group code 06-01)

> a. The derating requirements in 6.17.2 (below) are only applicable to Cermet types. The application and the
>    deratings of other fuse technologies shall be justified.

## 6.17.2 Derating, and Table 6-17

> a. Parameters of Fuses from family-group code 06-01 shall be derated as per Table 6-17.

**Table 6-17, Derating of parameters for Fuses family-group code 06-01**, read off the published figure:

| parameter | load ratio or limit |
|---|---|
| Current | **65 %** of the rated current, flat, up to a case temperature of **85 C**; falling linearly from 65 % at 85 C to **50 %** at **110 C**; nothing above 110 C |

## 6.17.3 Additional requirements not related to derating

> a. Fuses shall be avoided whenever possible.
>
> b. The largest fuse rating compatible with the source capability shall be used.
>
> c. The power supply shall be capable of delivering three times the specified fuse rated current in order to
>    obtain short fusing times.

## What this project may and may not conclude from it

**May.** Clauses 6.17.3 b and c are technology-independent statements about the CIRCUIT and this kit's fuses
are in exactly the circuit they describe: a source, a fuse, and a fault beyond it. Clause c is measurable here
and is measured, because `pcb_energy_chain.yaml` already carries the available fault current at each fuse.

**May not, without saying so.** The 65 percent of Table 6-17 is stated for **Cermet** fuses and this kit's are
automotive blade fuses; the standard's own 6.17.1a requires the application and derating of another technology
to be JUSTIFIED. So the 65 percent is used here as a SCREEN with its origin named, not as a limit this project
can claim the standard sets for a blade fuse. A blade fuse that carries less than 65 percent of its rating is
inside a criterion a space standard sets for a fuse of another construction, which is a defensible place to
be; one that carries more is not thereby non-compliant with anything, and the rule says which of the two it is
found.

**Nothing here is a fusing-time or an I2t requirement.** The standard gives no melting curve and no
coordination method; the curves this project uses are the fuse makers' own, on file per part.
